headline: 6 children die with measles symptoms in 24 hours
summary: The death toll has risen to 615 children since March 15, according to a report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Six children died within 24 hours (from Friday 8 AM to Saturday 8 AM) exhibiting symptoms of measles, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the total number of deaths due to measles symptoms since March 15 to 615, while 93 deaths have been confirmed as measles cases.
In the last 24 hours, 744 suspected measles cases were reported, and 45 cases were confirmed.
Since March 15, the total number of suspected measles cases has reached 98,266, while confirmed cases stand at 11,594.

In the last 24 hours, 744 suspected measles cases were reported, and 45 cases were confirmed.

headline_marked: 500+ ships stranded: [[UN works to restart evacuations]] in Strait of Hormuz
headline: 500+ ships stranded: UN works to restart evacuations in Strait of Hormuz
summary: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is negotiating with Iran, the US, and Oman to resume the safe passage of thousands of seafarers after a container ship attack.
details: The United Nations is working to resume the evacuation of hundreds of ships and thousands of stranded seafarers from the Strait of Hormuz after the process was halted earlier this week.
The International Maritime Organization (IMO) temporarily paused its evacuation initiative following an attack on a container ship operated by Taiwan's Evergreen.
IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez told a virtual news conference that 115 vessels and approximately 2,500 seafarers had successfully sailed through the strait before the pause.
Dominguez stated he is working vigilantly with Oman, the United States, and Iran to secure guarantees that vessels will not be targeted, though no specific timeframe for resumption has been provided.
Tehran has reasserted its right to control shipping in the critical waterway and warned Gulf neighbors against siding with Washington.
The IMO is currently investigating the reasons and motivations behind the ship attack that caused the evacuation pause.
The evacuation plan utilizes two channels: Iranian waters in the north and Omani waters in the south, following the 1968 Traffic Separation Scheme.
The central section of the strait is currently unusable due to the presence of an estimated 80 explosive mines, according to the IMO.
Over 500 vessels still need to be evacuated from the region, a process that is expected to take several weeks once operations resume.
caption:
Over 500 ships and thousands of seafarers remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a ship attack halted UN evacuations.

The United Nations is working to resume the evacuation of hundreds of ships and thousands of stranded seafarers from the Strait of Hormuz after the process was halted earlier this week.

The International Maritime Organization (IMO) temporarily paused its evacuation initiative following an attack on a container ship operated by Taiwan's Evergreen.

IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez told a virtual news conference that 115 vessels and approximately 2,500 seafarers had successfully sailed through the strait before the pause.

Dominguez stated he is working vigilantly with Oman, the United States, and Iran to secure guarantees that vessels will not be targeted, though no specific timeframe for resumption has been provided.

Tehran has reasserted its right to control shipping in the critical waterway and warned Gulf neighbors against siding with Washington.

The IMO is currently investigating the reasons and motivations behind the ship attack that caused the evacuation pause.

The evacuation plan utilizes two channels: Iranian waters in the north and Omani waters in the south, following the 1968 Traffic Separation Scheme.

The central section of the strait is currently unusable due to the presence of an estimated 80 explosive mines, according to the IMO.

Over 500 vessels still need to be evacuated from the region, a process that is expected to take several weeks once operations resume.
